problem:
Find the slope $m$ of the tangent line to the polar curve $r=1+\operatorname{sec}⁡(\theta )$ at $\theta =\frac{\pi }{3}$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\theta ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+{sec}^{2}⁡(\theta ), \\ {x}^{′}(\theta ) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Do not round the answer.

$m=$ 
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ we use the rule

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )}.
$$

We have,

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})+{sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+{2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+4 \\  & =\frac{9}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Hence, the slope $m$ of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =\pi /3} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})}{{x}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{9}{2})}{(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})} \\  & =-\frac{9}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =-3\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
